PAPERS.short: Sim real-time dust monitor bias gravimetric meta-analysis 2026
PAPERS.title: Systematic bias in real-time dust monitoring: a meta-analysis of measurement discrepancy and its implications for occupational exposure assessment.
PAPERS.pm: Optical real-time dust monitors (DustTrak, SidePak, pDR) vs gravimetric samplers
PAPERS.endpoint: Log response ratio of geometric-mean concentration, RTM vs gravimetric
PAPERS.n: PRISMA meta-analysis of 112 occupational studies; 96 paired RTM-gravimetric comparisons pooled in a three-level random-effects model. Professional photometers read 36% high on average: pooled lnR 0.31 (0.25-0.37), I2 78.4%, prediction interval 0.11-0.63. Factory-calibrated units read 43% high, site-calibrated units 13% high; site-specific calibration was the strongest moderator (beta -0.24, P<0.001), followed by log GSD of the size distribution (beta 0.15) and RH (beta 0.002 per %). No eligible study compared sub-$500 sensors against gravimetry. Limitation: geometric-mean ratios from heterogeneous aerosols and campaign lengths; the prediction interval never crosses zero but its width means a single uncalibrated deployment can be off by 12-88%. Relevance: high - the size-distribution and RH moderators are the same terms LCS calibration models need, now with a pooled prior.

PAPERS.short: Wang electret HVAC filter charge neutralisation wildfire smoke 2026
PAPERS.title: Charge-Driven Degradation of Residential Electret HVAC Filters under Wildfire Smoke Exposure.
PAPERS.pm: Flaming/smouldering wood smoke, prescribed-burn smoke and soot challenges; EPA monitor PM2.5 for model inputs
PAPERS.geo: United States (laboratory, prescribed burns, regional wildfire scenario)
PAPERS.endpoint: Electret filter fractional efficiency vs loading; modelled indoor PM2.5 protection
PAPERS.n: Laboratory flaming and smouldering wood smoke, field sampling at prescribed burns and controlled soot challenges on residential electret HVAC filters. Filtration efficiency collapsed at particle loadings far below those that raise pressure drop; the driver was soot-rich particles neutralising electret charge irreversibly, not mechanical clogging or organic-aerosol deposition. Built into a dynamic indoor model driven by EPA monitor data for a regional wildfire event, effective filter life fell from months to days at moderate outdoor PM2.5, with protection varying by building and ventilation. No efficiency numbers are given in the abstract. Limitation: few filter products and smoke types; charge loss in the field depends on soot fraction, which varies by fire stage. Relevance: high - indoor/outdoor LCS pairs can detect the efficiency collapse that pressure-based replacement rules miss.

PAPERS.short: Meng traffic noise air pollution lung function randomised crossover 2026
PAPERS.title: Independent and interactive effects of traffic-related noise and air pollution on lung function: A randomized crossover study in healthy young adults.
PAPERS.pm: Roadside PM1, PM2.5, PM10, O3, NO2 and noise during evening rush hour
PAPERS.endpoint: FVC, FEV1, FEV1/FVC, FEF25-75 and distal flows
PAPERS.n: Randomised crossover with four exposure conditions (noise and air pollution separated by intervention) in 51 healthy young adults beside a busy road at evening rush hour; pollutants and noise measured each session, mixed models adjusted for age, sex and BMI. Per 10 ug/m3 PM10, FEF75 fell 0.215 L/s; per 10 ug/m3 O3, 0.224 L/s. Noise independently reduced dynamic ventilatory indices, and exploratory interaction terms suggested noise amplified PM1- and PM2.5-associated FEV1 and small-airway decrements. No CIs in the abstract. Limitation: the four interventions are not described in the abstract and exposure conditions cannot be blinded, and pollutant contrasts within a single rush-hour session are small and collinear, so the interaction findings are hypothesis-generating. Relevance: medium - co-located acoustic and PM nodes are needed to separate the two stressors.

PAPERS.short: Liu PM2.5 components small for gestational age IVF Guangzhou 2026
PAPERS.title: Maternal exposure to PM(2.5) and its components and risk of small for gestational age in women undergoing in vitro fertilization: a propensity score-matched case-control study in Guangzhou, China.
PAPERS.pm: Trimester-averaged PM2.5 and SO4, NO3, NH4, OM, BC (gridded estimates at residence)
PAPERS.endpoint: Small for gestational age in IVF pregnancies
PAPERS.n: Propensity-score-matched case-control within 1,459 IVF conceptions in Guangzhou: 166 SGA cases matched 1:1. Whole-pregnancy PM2.5 OR 1.124 (1.015-1.245); second trimester 1.082 (1.005-1.165); third trimester 1.075 (1.002-1.154); the exposure increment is not given in the abstract. SO4, OM and BC were positively associated; mixture models ranked nitrate as the dominant driver, and no subgroup reached significance. Limitation: 332 matched women give lower CI bounds within 0.2-1.5% of the null across many component-by-window tests, with no multiplicity correction reported; the component estimates come from a modelled product whose component-specific error is unknown. Relevance: low-medium - component attribution here rests on modelled speciation that sensor networks cannot supply.

PAPERS.short: Wang seasonal PM size constituents oxylipin panel Beijing 2026
PAPERS.title: Winter and Summer Differences in Oxylipin Responses to Ambient Particles: Roles of Sizes and Constituents
PAPERS.pm: 27 PM2.5 metrics: mass, UFP and accumulation-mode number, OC, chloride and other constituents
PAPERS.endpoint: Circulating LTB4 and 5-, 8-, 12-, 15-HETE
PAPERS.n: Panel of 123 adults in Beijing with repeated visits in winter and summer; 27 PM2.5 mass, size and constituent metrics against five lipoxygenase-derived oxylipins. Associations peaked at lag 0-1 d; across metrics, oxylipin increases ranged 3.3-114.2%, most robust for UFP, accumulation-mode number, OC and chloride. UFP showed an exposure-response only in summer: per IQR, +12.9 to +97.7% in summer vs -7.7 to +18.8% in winter; accumulation-mode and OC effects were larger in winter. No CIs in the abstract. Limitation: 27 metrics x 5 biomarkers x 2 seasons x several lags is a large test space, and the season contrast also changes time outdoors and ventilation. Relevance: high - size-resolved number, not mass, carries the summer signal, which mass-only optical sensors cannot report.

PAPERS.short: Langford cooking dominant primary PM1 eddy covariance London Beijing Delhi 2026
PAPERS.title: Traffic and combustion emission controls leave cooking as a dominant local source of primary PM1 in megacities
PAPERS.design: Eddy covariance flux measurement, method development
PAPERS.pm: Chemically resolved non-refractory PM1 fluxes (aerosol mass spectrometry + eddy covariance)
PAPERS.endpoint: Source-attributed primary PM1 emission fluxes
PAPERS.n: Eddy-covariance fluxes with aerosol mass spectrometry and a new source-attribution method in three megacity neighbourhoods. In Delhi, traffic and combustion dominate primary PM1 emission. In London and Beijing, cooking is the largest local primary source at mealtimes: up to 83% of midday and 87% of early-evening emission in London, 61% and 76% in Beijing. Cooking is absent from national, European and global inventories, though the London Atmospheric Emissions Inventory's estimate matched. Primary emission sources differ from those controlling ambient PM1 mass, which is secondary-dominated. Limitation: one flux footprint per city and non-refractory PM1 only (no BC or dust). Relevance: high - source-resolved flux benchmarks for inventory checks; cooking plumes are a known optical-sensor artefact at street level.

PAPERS.short: Sun respirable mining dust natural killer cell dysfunction 2026
PAPERS.title: Respirable Particulate Matter Induces Natural Killer Cell Dysfunction via Oxidative Stress-Mediated Lysosomal and Mitochondrial Injury: Implications for Mineral-Rich Mining Dust Exposure.
PAPERS.pm: Compositionally distinct respirable PM (silica/silicate, iron-bearing, carbonaceous mine dusts)
PAPERS.endpoint: NK-cell viability, cytokines, perforin/granzyme B, K562 killing
PAPERS.n: In-vitro exposure of NK cells to respirable mineral dusts with a K562 target-cell challenge. Injury was dose- and composition-dependent: apoptosis/necrosis, shifted cytokines, altered perforin/granzyme B function and impaired killing. Silica- and silicate-rich dusts were worst; iron-bearing and carbonaceous dusts produced distinct oxidative patterns. Mitochondrial depolarisation, lower mitochondrial mass and lysosomal deacidification converged across dusts; ascorbic acid partially restored organelle function and IFN-gamma. Doses and their relation to inhaled lung burden are not given in the abstract. Limitation: an isolated cell line in submerged culture, no lung-burden dosimetry, so the proposed adverse outcome pathway to lung cancer is inferential. Relevance: low - composition (silica fraction) matters, which mass sensors cannot resolve. Note: this DOI was held from the 3 Oct issue as unauthored and is now carried here.

PAPERS.short: Liang emergency haze controls causal ML synthetic control Shijiazhuang 2026
PAPERS.title: Evaluating Emergency Emission Controls During an Unprecedented Regional Haze Event Using Causal Machine Learning
PAPERS.pm: Monitor PM2.5, PM10, SO2, NO2, CO; PM2.5 source apportionment
PAPERS.endpoint: Intervention-attributable emission strength and concentration change
PAPERS.n: Three-step causal evaluation (meteorological normalisation, augmented synthetic control, ML prediction) of Shijiazhuang's 45-day 'Sharp Sword' campaign in 2016. Local emission strength fell 4.3% (PM2.5), 4.8% (PM10), 15.8% (SO2), 5.8% (NO2), 15.3% (CO); concentrations fell 42.1 ug/m3 (14.8%) for PM2.5 and 47.4 ug/m3 (12.4%) for PM10. Independent PMF showed vehicle, steelmaking and coal contributions 4.1%, 11.0% and 21.7% lower than in 2017. PM2.5 still averaged 243.2 ug/m3 during the campaign. Limitation: donor-city synthetic controls share the regional haze and possibly spillover controls, biasing the effect toward zero; no uncertainty intervals in the abstract. Relevance: medium - a transferable counterfactual framework for evaluating interventions from network data.

PAPERS.short: Perez-Vizcaino PM10 sources Riotinto mining multi-time-resolution PMF 2026
PAPERS.title: Characterization of PM(10) sources in the Riotinto copper mining district (SW Spain) using multi-time-resolution receptor modelling.
PAPERS.design: Intensive field campaign, PMF source apportionment
PAPERS.pm: Hourly XRF elements and Aethalometer BC + daily filter PM10 chemistry
PAPERS.endpoint: PM10 source contributions
PAPERS.n: Year-long (July 2024-July 2025) campaign combining an hourly XRF metals monitor and an Aethalometer with daily high-volume quartz-filter chemistry, merged in multi-time-resolution PMF. Seven sources: waste rock 4.9, regional + traffic 3.6, open pit 1.6, combustion 1.2, aged marine 1.2, dust 1.1 and copper concentrate 0.7 ug/m3. Daily species identified traffic tracers and SOA that the hourly subset alone missed. Arsenic was the main geochemical anomaly. Limitation: one receptor site; multi-resolution PMF weights the daily data heavily and factor uncertainty (bootstrap/DISP) is not reported in the abstract. Relevance: medium - hourly XRF + BC is the reference tier that low-cost networks around mines would need to be anchored to for metal-rich dust.

PAPERS.short: Chen primary brown carbon China 2005-2020 trends radiative effect 2026
PAPERS.title: Long-term evolution and effects of primary brown carbon aerosol in China
PAPERS.pm: Modelled primary brown carbon (internal-mixing optical model), PM2.5
PAPERS.endpoint: Surface and column PBrC, sector shares, direct radiative effect
PAPERS.n: CTM simulation of primary BrC across China, 2005-2020, with an internal-mixing optical model. Mean surface PBrC 0.81 ugC/m3; residential, industrial and agricultural combustion contributed 57%, 22% and 18%, together 91% of column PBrC in 2010. PBrC fell 20.8% over the period vs 8.1% for PM2.5; direct radiative effect fell from +0.032 to +0.023 W/m2 (-25.7%), 84.2% anthropogenic. Limitation: BrC emission factors and absorption Angstrom exponents are poorly constrained, and evaluation against measured absorption is not described in the abstract. Relevance: medium - multi-wavelength absorption (BrC) channels on sensor nodes could test the residential-combustion dominance.

PAPERS.short: Srivastav ion particle size distribution NPF Indo-Gangetic Plain 2026
PAPERS.title: Ion and particle size distribution measurements in the Indo-Gangetic Plain: seasonal insights and challenges in new particle formation event characterization
PAPERS.pm: Air-ion (0.8-42 nm) and particle (2.5-42 nm) size distributions
PAPERS.endpoint: NPF event frequency, condensation sink, growth rates
PAPERS.n: Ion and particle spectrometer measurements at a suburban IGP site, May-December 2023. NPF occurred on 30/35 valid days (86%) in May-June but 20/73 (28%) in winter/post-monsoon. Morning median condensation sink was lower on event days (0.0095 vs 0.0292 s-1). Growth rates rose with size, 14.7 nm/h (3-7 nm) to 19.0 nm/h (7-20 nm). Pollution plumes intermittently masked or distorted events, so both visual and automated classification and growth-rate fitting were unreliable. Limitation: no precursor gas (H2SO4, amines, HOMs) measurements, so mechanism is unconstrained; eight months at one site. Relevance: medium - in high-CS settings the UFP number seen by condensation or diffusion-charger sensors is plume- not nucleation-driven.

PAPERS.short: Kuye ultrafine particle respiratory deposition dose wood stoves UK homes 2026
PAPERS.title: Respiratory Deposition Dose of Ultrafine Particles from Improved Wood Stoves and Open Fireplaces
PAPERS.pm: Indoor particle number concentration (1-min) with ICRP deposition model
PAPERS.endpoint: Inhaled and respiratory-deposited UFP dose
PAPERS.n: Exploratory measurements in four UK homes (Ecodesign stove, multifuel Ecodesign stove x2, open fireplace), 11-12 winter days each, 1-min PNC combined with age/sex/activity ventilation rates and the ICRP model. Daily inhaled dose 0.45-16.0 x10^9 particles/kg/day sitting and 2.37-73.2 x10^9 at moderate activity (4.5-5.3-fold higher). Child scenarios had 2.7-3.8x the adult body-mass-normalised dose; household mean deposition rate 1.50-5.99 x10^8 particles/min. Limitation: n=4 homes that differ simultaneously in appliance, fuel, room, ventilation and behaviour, so stove-type effects cannot be identified; doses are modelled from concentration, not measured. Relevance: medium - residential UFP is invisible to mass sensors; indoor PNC nodes are the relevant instrument.

PAPERS.short: Stange SEM-Raman inhalable particles indoor artificial turf infill 2026
PAPERS.title: Correlative SEM–Raman Microscopy of Inhalable Particles Sampled during Indoor Football on Artificial Turf with Crumb Rubber and Olive-Stone Infills
PAPERS.pm: PM10 mass; single-particle SEM + AI classification + micro-Raman of airborne dust
PAPERS.endpoint: Infill-derived airborne particle composition and PM10
PAPERS.n: Air sampling during matches in two Norwegian indoor halls, one with crumb-rubber infill and one with olive-stone/quartz infill, analysed by correlative SEM, AI particle classification and micro-Raman. Both infills released airborne particles. Olive-stone particles appeared indoors only; tyre rubber appeared indoors and outdoors, implicating traffic as well as infill. PM10 was 58.4 ug/m3 in the olive-stone hall vs 6.0 ug/m3 with crumb rubber, and fungal spores were found with the organic infill. Limitation: one hall per infill, so the tenfold PM10 difference is confounded by hall ventilation, occupancy and cleaning. Preprint. Relevance: low-medium - substituting a 'sustainable' material changed composition and raised mass.

PAPERS.short: Wang multi-omics Mendelian randomization PM2.5 depression 2026
PAPERS.title: Multi-omics Mendelian Randomization Reveals the Causal Association and Mediating Mechanisms of PM2.5 with Depression: A Systematic Study Integrating Transcriptomics, Metabolomics, and Radiomics
PAPERS.pm: Genetically predicted PM2.5 exposure (GWAS instruments)
PAPERS.endpoint: Major depressive disorder; omics mediators
PAPERS.n: LD-score regression found genetic correlation between 'PM2.5 exposure' and MDD (rg 0.334, P 1.9e-11); two-sample MR gave OR 1.27 (1.07-1.51) for MDD. Two-step MR identified five blood genes, six brain-region genes and two blood fatty-acid ratios as mediators; no mediation through CSF metabolites or imaging traits. Limitation: a GWAS of residential PM2.5 indexes where people live, so its instruments capture SES, urbanicity and migration; the genetic correlation itself shows horizontal pleiotropy with MDD is likely, which violates the exclusion restriction. The OR has no exposure unit. Preprint. Relevance: low - not an exposure-measurement result.

PAPERS.short: Guerra-Ruiz cytokines volcanic emissions Cumbre Vieja ASHES 2026
PAPERS.title: Systemic cytokine signatures associated with volcanic emisions exposure and respiratory disease after the cumbre vieja eruption-ashes project.
PAPERS.pm: Volcanic gas and particulate exposure (hours of exposure, group membership)
PAPERS.endpoint: Serum TH1/TH2/TH17 biomarkers (48-plex Olink)
PAPERS.n: Cross-sectional ASHES sub-study after the 2021 Tajogaite eruption: 102 adults (66 general population, 13 occupationally exposed, 23 asthmatic). Workers had the longest exposure (median 10 h vs 6 h) and higher IL-2, IL-7, IL-17A and IL-17F; asthmatics showed broader TH1/TH2/TH17 activation, and IL-4 correlated with exposure time in asthmatics (r 0.79). Limitation: exposure is hours of presence, not measured PM or SO2, and 13 workers is too few for a stable comparison; 48 markers tested without stated correction. Relevance: medium - the eruption had dense monitoring; linking those PM records to individuals would turn this into an exposure-response study.

PAPERS.short: Mohammed mobile HEPA-UV air decontamination operating theatre 2026
PAPERS.title: Evaluation of a mobile surgical air decontamination device in reducing airborne microbial load in the operating theatre of a tertiary care hospital.
PAPERS.pm: Optical particle counts (0.3, 0.5 um and larger) and culturable CFU
PAPERS.endpoint: Particle count and airborne microbial load
PAPERS.n: Before-after evaluation of a mobile HEPA + UV decontamination unit in one operating theatre over 15 days (July 2025). Mean total particle count fell from 6,836 to 4,072 particles/m3 (-40.4%), significant in the 0.3 and 0.5 um channels; CFU fell from 34.5 to 15.2 CFU/m3 (P 0.003). Limitation: one theatre, short before-after design with no control period or blinding to activity level, and no clinical outcome (surgical-site infection). Relevance: low-medium - shows optical counters as the performance metric for portable cleaners in clinical rooms.

PAPERS.short: Liu PM2.5 sources mixing state Chengdu Kangding altitude 2026
PAPERS.title: Altitudinal and seasonal differences in PM(2.5) sources, secondary formation, and particle mixing states in the basin-plateau transition zone of Southwest China.
PAPERS.pm: Filter PM2.5 chemistry (ions, carbon) and single-particle mass spectrometry
PAPERS.endpoint: PM2.5 composition, PMF sources, mixing state
PAPERS.n: Summer and winter PM2.5 sampling at Chengdu (500 m) and Kangding (2,500 m). Winter PM2.5 79.4 vs 15.2 ug/m3, summer 29.1 vs 8.1. Inorganic ions dominated in Chengdu, carbonaceous species in Kangding; sulfate in summer gave way to nitrate in winter. PMF: Chengdu combustion 26.0%, traffic 32.4%, secondary 35.3%; Kangding combustion 47.9%. Single-particle data showed more SIA particles in Chengdu (29.0% vs 17.6%) and more organic-SIA internal mixing in Kangding. Limitation: two seasons, two sites; the altitude contrast is confounded with city size and heating fuel. Relevance: low - descriptive regional chemistry.

PAPERS.short: Ghosh meter-scale heterogeneity new particle formation 3D model 2026
PAPERS.title: How Microscale Flow and Vapor Transport Shape New Particle Formation and Growth.
PAPERS.pm: Simulated nucleation-mode particle number and size distributions (3D-ICAM, 10 m resolution)
PAPERS.endpoint: Nucleation intensity, sub-3 nm growth rates, size distributions
PAPERS.n: A 10 m resolution 3D multiphysics aerosol model (3D-ICAM) compared with an equivalent box model across emission geometries. Under weak winds (<1 m/s), it reproduced nucleation hotspots, intermittent multi-episode nucleation and persistent bimodal size distributions that the homogeneous case lacks. Resolving spatial structure raised predicted sub-3 nm growth rates up to ~20-fold, bringing them into the observed range, because transport-generated microenvironments relax the growth-scavenging competition. Limitation: idealised geometries; agreement with observations is at the level of growth-rate ranges, not site-specific validation. Relevance: medium - implies point UFP measurements in streets sample sub-grid hotspots; dense number-sensor networks are the natural test.

PAPERS.short: Zhang early-onset female lung cancer burden GBD 2021 2026
PAPERS.title: Global Burden and Trends of Early-Onset Tracheal, Bronchus, and Lung Cancer Among Women From 1990 to 2021.
PAPERS.pm: Ambient particulate matter pollution (GBD risk factor)
PAPERS.endpoint: Early-onset female tracheal, bronchus and lung cancer ASIR, ASDR, DALYs
PAPERS.n: GBD 2021 secondary analysis of early-onset (under 50) female TBL cancer, 1990-2021. Global rates declined (all EAPCs <0), but low-middle SDI regions rose (DALY EAPC 0.66) and South Asia fastest (DALY EAPC 1.42). Ambient PM was the fastest-growing attributable risk (attributable DALY rate EAPC 1.22, ASDR 1.27). Limitation: GBD attributable burden is model output that inherits the exposure surface and IER curves; in young women with few cases, estimates in low-SDI regions rest largely on modelled covariates rather than registries. Relevance: low - burden, not measurement.

PAPERS.short: Cantu air quality across the lifespan nursing response review 2026
PAPERS.title: Breathing Unequal Air: Global and US Air Quality Across the Lifespan and the Nursing Response.
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5, O3, NO2 (reviewed)
PAPERS.endpoint: Cardiopulmonary, neurocognitive and perinatal morbidity (reviewed)
PAPERS.n: Narrative review for nurses of global and US air quality trends and health effects across the lifespan, citing ~8 million deaths/year attributable to air pollution, with PM2.5, O3 and NO2 as the principal pollutants. Covers cardiopulmonary, neurocognitive and perinatal outcomes, nursing practice and policy, and argues for integrating air-quality awareness into nursing curricula. No new data. Limitation: non-systematic; no synthesis of effect sizes. Relevance: low - possible audience for patient-facing use of public sensor maps.

PAPERS.short: Atkin air quality excess heat pregnancy outcomes review 2026
PAPERS.title: Impact of Poor Air Quality and Excess Heat on Pregnancy Outcomes.
PAPERS.pm: Ambient air pollution and heat (reviewed)
PAPERS.endpoint: Adverse pregnancy outcomes (reviewed)
PAPERS.n: Narrative review on combined poor air quality and excess heat in pregnancy. Argues that physiological adaptations of pregnancy raise susceptibility, that structural determinants concentrate exposure in some populations, and that nurses should educate patients, promote adaptation and advocate for climate mitigation. No quantitative synthesis in the abstract. Limitation: non-systematic; heat-pollution interaction is asserted rather than quantified. Relevance: low - clinical guidance context only.

PAPERS.short: Cai self-supervised stacking particulate nitrate sparse observations 2026
PAPERS.title: A Self-supervised Stacking Framework for Estimating Particulate Nitrate in Two Chinese Urban Agglomerations under Sparse Ground Observations
PAPERS.pm: Particulate nitrate (estimated from sparse ground observations)
PAPERS.endpoint: Gridded particulate nitrate estimates
PAPERS.n: Title and authors only (Cai, He, Li, Liu et al.). No abstract was retrievable from Crossref, Europe PMC or Semantic Scholar at harvest. The title describes a self-supervised stacking ensemble that estimates particulate nitrate in two Chinese urban agglomerations from sparse ground observations. Predictors, validation design and skill cannot be stated. Limitation: unverifiable beyond the title; with sparse speciation sites, random cross-validation would overstate skill (see the 22 Oct blocked-CV record). Relevance: medium - component estimation under sparse reference sites is the same problem as filling between LCS anchors.

PAPERS.short: Kaskaoutis in situ aerosol optical properties eastern Mediterranean 2026
PAPERS.title: In situ aerosol optical properties in the background eastern Mediterranean: seasonal variability, regional transport, and source attribution
PAPERS.pm: In situ aerosol scattering and absorption
PAPERS.endpoint: Seasonal aerosol optical properties and source attribution
PAPERS.n: Title and authors only (Kaskaoutis, Baalbaki, Bimenyimana et al.). No abstract was retrievable at harvest. The title describes in situ scattering/absorption measurements at a background eastern Mediterranean site, with seasonal variability, regional transport and source attribution. Site, instruments and values cannot be stated. Limitation: unverifiable beyond the title. Relevance: low-medium - background optical properties set the mass-scattering efficiency that optical PM sensors assume.

PAPERS.short: Zhao PM2.5-O3 co-pollution episodes BTH YRD 2026
PAPERS.title: Episode analysis of the characteristics and causes of PM2.5–O3 co-pollution in Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei and Yangtze River Delta, China
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 and O3 co-pollution episodes (monitoring data)
PAPERS.endpoint: Characteristics and causes of co-pollution episodes
PAPERS.n: Title and authors only (Zhao, Xu, Gao, Zhang et al.). No abstract was retrievable at harvest. The title describes an episode analysis of simultaneous PM2.5 and O3 exceedance in BTH and the YRD, including causes. Data sources, period and attribution method cannot be stated. Limitation: unverifiable beyond the title. Relevance: low-medium - co-pollution episodes are where PM-only alerts from sensor networks understate risk.
